new_statements.relation_note: Three-level tone system; nasalised vowels; implosives; labio-velars. No statement on stress/accent. Also: 955-entry lexical database with dialect labels Gangumi vs Garba Chede; IPA transcriptions (3-3.5 h) and 27-30 min glossed; practical orthography in development.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Jirim is a tone language with three level tones (three-level tone system); nothing is said about word stress or accent.
new_statements.exceptions: none; no detail on contour tones, downstep or tone-bearing unit (the collection holds ~3.5 h of IPA transcription and a 955-entry FLEx lexicon; 'the grammatical analysis is still at an early stage')
new_statements.identity_note: Explicitly Jirim of Taraba State, Bali and Gashaka LGAs (Garba Chede, Gangumi, Kufai, Kankani; Gandole/Kwagiri named as Jirim-area villages = Meek's 'Dirrim of Kwagiri'); the description itself cites Glottolog diri1253, Meek 1931 and Migeod 1925 as the only prior sources, and distinguishes Jirim from 'the closely related Chamba Daka (Boyd & Sa'ad 2010)'. Depositor's own fieldwork (June-July 2023; Feb-May 2025; ELDP page adds Nov-Dec 2025). Not a namesake. Live ELAR page is behind an automated-access block JS challenge; the Internet Archive copy of 2026-01-20 was read and. Companion records seen (not separate works): ELDP project register id 3266 and cultureincrisis.org project page (planned outputs: grammar sketch, practical orthography, Jirim-Hausa-English dictionary, text collection - none released yet).

sources.note: About Chamba Daka (Sámá mum, samb1311), not Dirim: 'Tones: Chamba has three "registers": high, medium (or mid), and low.. The representation of Chamba tone is complicated by.. "downstep"' (p. 31). Consonants, 8 vowels, vowel length described; no statement on stress or accent. p. 2: 'No modern linguistic studies of this language have been published'.
